status: Exploratory locally specified analysis before inspecting new integrated FQI channel outcomes; prior dialogue, policy and rule-channel outcomes were already inspected. Not preregistration or an untouched external holdout.
question: When does optional bargaining add value relative to the same customer's ordinary checkout opportunity, and do conditional negotiation rankings carry over to channel-value rankings?
input: Frozen rule and five-seed full/clock FQI potential trajectories from integration/results. Original source data and earlier results remain untouched. No policy retraining or test-based tuning.
selection_sensitivity: Value-dependent odds multiply base odds by 2 below listing and by .5 at or above listing. This is a stipulated composition change, not inferred or endogenous choice, and private values are not policy inputs.
estimands: Incremental seller net surplus per original opportunity
Incremental buyer net surplus per original opportunity
Minimum fallback probability at fixed costs
Conditional composition and policy-cost crossing thresholds
analysis_unit: Average 80 repetitions within each product and equally average the five frozen training seeds for learned policies before product comparisons. Rules have one deterministic policy instance. Every comparison pairs the same 193 products and underlying customer opportunities. Seeds and trajectories are not independent shoppers.
intervals: 2000 paired product bootstrap resamples, seed 20261002. Compute intervals for each policy at p=.5, r=.5, c_s=c_b=.005 in both selection mechanisms and all 12 behavioral conditions, and fixed full-minus-time/full-minus-clock contrasts. Cost and fallback thresholds use bootstrap ratios of average coefficients, not averages of individual ratios. Do not drop or clip infeasible thresholds. Report zero-denominator cases explicitly; bootstrap undefined fraction is retained. Full factorial grid receives point estimates, avoiding redundant thousands of interval estimates.

threshold_equations.seller_increment: A_s + r U_s - c_s H, with A_s=E[q(S-S0)], U_s=E[q(1-D)S0], H=E[qT]
threshold_equations.buyer_increment: A_b + r U_b - c_b H, with A_b=E[q(B-B0)], U_b=E[q(1-D)B0]
threshold_equations.cost_ceiling: (A_j+r U_j)/H for H>0; a negative ceiling means no nonnegative variable interaction cost supports a nonnegative average increment
threshold_equations.fallback_floor: (c_j H-A_j)/U_j for U_j>0; <=0 means no fallback required, (0,1] feasible, >1 infeasible. When U_j=0 fallback cannot change the increment
threshold_equations.exogenous_opt_in: For constant p>0 every incremental term is p times a fixed conditional coefficient. Sign and variable-cost/fallback thresholds do not depend on p. No nontrivial uptake threshold is claimed without composition change or additional fixed costs
threshold_equations.composition: For odds-weighted selection, q_low=2p/(1+p) and q_high=p/(2-p). If G_low and G_high are unconditional opportunity-weighted incremental coefficients within each eligibility group, total increment is q_low G_low+q_high G_high. Nonzero crossing p*=(4G_low+G_high)/(2G_low-G_high), retained only as an algebraic boundary with explicit feasible-domain checks
threshold_equations.policy_cost_crossing: For policies a,b at common p,r and a fixed selection mechanism, seller difference is delta_gross-c_s delta_rounds. A positive interior crossing c*=delta_gross/delta_rounds can reverse the ranking; if delta_rounds=0 no finite crossing is identified. Report all pairwise coefficients/crossings and directions rather than test-selecting a favorable example

negative_control_and_illustration: Added before reading integrated outcomes: with identical constant positive opt-in, zero costs and zero fallback, pairwise incremental seller differences must be p times pairwise gross negotiation-surplus differences, because the same checkout baseline cancels. Subtraction alone cannot reverse rankings. A separately labeled analytical fixture uses a below-listing customer with floor .70, value .95, policy A price .90 and six rounds, policy B price .88 and one round, opt-in .5 and no fallback. Gross seller surplus favors A (.20 versus .18), but cost .005 per round favors B (.085 versus .0875 incremental surplus); exact crossing .004. This is constructed arithmetic, not an observed simulation result or a policy selected on outcomes.
regret: Descriptive hindsight opportunity loss relative to the best mean among four frozen bargaining policies and checkout-only, separately for each stipulated design. Not a learned selector, a regret guarantee, a deployment recommendation or an inferential test of the selected winner. Report worst-condition regret across the declared finite conditions without optimizing parameters on these data.
verification: Independently enumerate direct-checkout, negotiation-sale, fallback-sale and non-purchase route probabilities. Reconstruct seller receipts minus proxy cost and buyer value minus payment in listing units; verify internal payments cancel in joint gross surplus and participant costs remain separate. Check all source deal/price bounds, seed counts, unique keys and matched latent opportunities. Check decomposition for every trajectory at the primary design and bounded edge cases, plus exogenous scaling, analytic threshold roots, explicit zero-denominator cases and aggregation identities. Compare frozen rule outputs with prior records on the identical stream. Use an alternate output directory for a complete analysis rerun.
claim_limits: Accounting implications are transparent consequences of fixed potential outcomes, not a newly discovered economic law or endogenous bargaining equilibrium. Neither simulation nor bootstrap establishes adoption, willingness to negotiate, actual profit, individual Pareto improvement, external validity or a causal customer effect. Merchant floors are proxies, not acquisition costs. Costs do not alter trajectories. Fallback represents aggregate re-engagement after failure. No extra fixed platform cost is introduced into the evaluated primary model.
